correctness.rationale: For F=E^{⊕m}, R=rm, the fixed-metric section algebra is the stated matrix amplification. Spectrum is the union of the fiber spectra (fiberwise inversion is continuous). Any finite separation of the compact spectrum into nonempty clopen groups gives nonzero algebraically orthogonal Riesz idempotents. If arbitrarily many components existed, compactness and equality of components and quasi-components would give arbitrarily large such separations. Their ranges are continuous constant-rank bundles on the connected sphere, so at most R groups are possible. A splitting conversely yields that spectrum via orthogonal projections: use a metric-orthogonal representative of the splitting, or transport by the unitary part of the splitting isomorphism to respect the fixed metric. The U(s+1)/U(s) sphere has dimension 2s+1, so stabilization on π_{2k−1} is an isomorphism for s≥k. Thus F is a rank-k bundle plus R−k trivial lines. Nonzero c_k multiplies by m, forces a summand of rank ≥k, and equality at R−k+1 forces the stated ranks. H²=0 makes lines trivial; Bott integrality is injective in the stable range, proving zero-Chern triviality and the uniqueness up to isomorphism claimed at equality. This also covers R=k, when one component is optimal. The proof is not a finite numerical verification.
